summary: Defines Multicast Router Discovery, a standard way for devices to find multicast routers. IGMP and MLD snooping switches need to know where routers are, but vendors used different methods, causing interoperability problems. This mechanism does not depend on any specific multicast routing protocol. It is on the standards track.

eli5.summary: Network switches need to know which neighbor is the one handing out broadcast shows. This memo gives a standard way for that neighbor to say hello.

subtitle: A standard way for switches that snoop on multicast traffic to find which neighbors are multicast routers.

tldr.problem: IGMP and MLD snooping switches must know where multicast routers are, but snooping is not standardized and vendors used different methods, causing interoperability problems.
tldr.mechanism: Three small messages sent over IGMP (IPv4) or MLD (IPv6): Advertisement from routers, Solicitation from devices, and Termination when a router stops forwarding.
tldr.outcome: Switches can track multicast routers without relying on any particular multicast routing protocol; security relies on link-local checks, rate limiting and optionally SEND or IPsec.

today: RFC 4286 is a Proposed Standard, and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why Routers Must Be Discoverable
sections.content:
Multicast Router Discovery (MRD) messages help determine which nodes attached to a switch have multicast routing enabled. This matters in a layer-2 bridging domain with snooping switches, which need to know where to send multicast source data and group membership messages. Source data and membership reports must be received by all multicast routers on a segment.

Using group membership Query messages to find routers is insufficient because of query suppression. MRD could have been built on ICMP, but the group management protocols were chosen because the function is multicast specific, and this lets operators see MRD problems alongside data forwarding problems.
sections.eli5: Switches need to know which neighbors pass multicast along. Asking the usual way does not always work, so there is a special hello message for it.

sections.title: Three Messages
sections.content:
MRD has three messages. A multicast router sends an Advertisement to say IP multicast forwarding is enabled. A device may send a Solicitation to ask routers to advertise. A router sends a Termination when it stops multicast routing on an interface.

Advertisements go out periodically on every interface with multicast forwarding enabled, and also in reply to Solicitations. They also carry group management variables, which can be used for consistency checking on the subnet. All MRD messages use an IPv4 TTL or IPv6 Hop Limit of 1 and carry the Router Alert Option (RFC 2113, RFC 2711). Advertisement and Termination go to the All-Snoopers multicast address; Solicitation goes to the All-Routers address. All messages SHOULD be rate-limited per MaxMessageRate, and any data beyond the fixed format MUST be ignored.
sections.eli5: There are three notes: "I am a router", "are there any routers?" and "I am quitting being a router". They only travel one hop, to the neighbors.

sections.title: Message Formats
sections.content:
The Advertisement has a Type, an Advertisement Interval, a Checksum, a Query Interval and a Robustness Variable. The Type is 0x30 for IPv4 and 151 for IPv6. The Advertisement Interval is the configured AdvertisementInterval in seconds. The Query Interval is the Querier's Query Interval (QQI, not the coded QQIC) in use by IGMP or MLD on the interface, or 0 if neither is enabled. The Robustness Variable comes from IGMPv2, IGMPv3 or MLD on the interface, or is 0 if IGMPv1 or no group protocol is in use.

Solicitation and Termination are shorter: Type, Reserved (set to 0 and ignored on reception) and Checksum. Solicitation uses 0x31 and 152; Termination uses 0x32 and 153. For IPv4 the checksum is the usual one's complement over the IGMP message with the checksum field set to 0; for IPv6 it is the ICMPv6 checksum. The IPv4 Protocol field is IGMP (2), and the IPv6 Next Header is 58. IPv6 source addresses MUST be link-local.
sections.eli5: Each note is tiny: a label saying which kind it is, a check number, and for the router's hello a couple of timing facts.

sections.title: Timers and Constants
sections.content:
An MRD implementation MUST support configuring these variables. AdvertisementInterval must be between 4 and 180 seconds, default 20. AdvertisementJitter randomizes timing so routers do not synchronize, and zero is discouraged. MaxInitialAdvertisementInterval defaults to 2 seconds and MaxInitialAdvertisements to 3. MaxMessageRate defaults to 10 messages per second.

A receiver sets NeighborDeadInterval to 3 times the sum of the received Advertisement Interval field plus the jitter computed from it; a neighbor with no Advertisement in that time is considered unreachable. Protocol constants are MAX_RESPONSE_DELAY of 2 seconds, MAX_SOLICITATION_DELAY of 1 second and MAX_SOLICITATIONS of 3 transmissions.
sections.eli5: Routers say hello about every 20 seconds, a little randomly. If a neighbor goes quiet for about three rounds, it is considered gone.

sections.title: Sending and Receiving
sections.content:
Advertisements are sent when the periodic timer fires, and after a short random delay when an interface is enabled, re-initialized or MRD is enabled (up to MaxInitialAdvertisements, for robustness against loss). On a Solicitation, a router replies after a random delay less than MAX_RESPONSE_DELAY, and ignores further Solicitations while one reply is pending. Changes to Query Interval or Robustness Variable MUST NOT trigger a new Advertisement, but the new values MUST be used afterwards.

Receivers validate Advertisements: correct checksum, destination equal to All-Snoopers and, for IPv6, a link-local source. Failures MUST be silently discarded. Solicitations are sent when an interface is initialized or MRD is enabled, to the All-Routers address.

Terminations are sent when forwarding or the interface is disabled, the router shuts down gracefully, or MRD is disabled. A receiver that validates a Termination sends a Solicitation, and removes the sender from its active router list if no Advertisement arrives within NeighborDeadInterval.
sections.eli5: Routers announce themselves when they wake up and now and then after. If one announces it is leaving, the others double-check by asking who is still there.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
MRD is link-local, so traffic from off-network sources should never be accepted. IPv6 messages MUST have a valid link-local source; IPv4 receivers MUST discard messages with a non-local source.

Spoofed Terminations are handled by validating them with a Solicitation. Spoofed Solicitations can be used for flooding, mitigated by rate limiting. A spoofed Advertisement lets a rogue machine pose as a router and eavesdrop or cause denial of service. The RFC points to SEND (RFC 3971) for IPv6, and to IPsec ESP (RFC 2406) with a null encryption algorithm and a keyed authentication algorithm such as HMAC-SHA-1 for IPv4 and IPv6, which needs a manually configured shared key and requires disabling replay protection.
sections.eli5: A fake sign could trick the mail sorter. The defenses are to only trust neighbors on the same hallway and, if needed, to check a secret handshake.

sections.title: Assigned Values
sections.content: IANA assigned three IGMP types (0x30, 0x31, 0x32) and three ICMPv6 types from the Informational range (151, 152, 153) for Advertisement, Solicitation and Termination. The IPv4 All-Snoopers address is 224.0.0.106, in the 224.0.0/24 link-local control range. The IPv6 address is FF02:0:0:0:0:0:0:6A, link-local in scope, with a group ID equal to the low-order 8 bits of the IPv4 address.
sections.eli5: Each note kind and the special shared address got official numbers so every vendor uses the same ones.

fields.name: Checksum
fields.desc: IGMP checksum for IPv4, ICMPv6 checksum for IPv6.

fields.name: Query Interval
fields.desc: IGMP or MLD Query Interval in seconds; 0 if not enabled.

fields.name: Robustness Variable
fields.desc: IGMPv2, IGMPv3 or MLD value; 0 if IGMPv1 or none.

messages.label: Advertisement
messages.note: Sent to All-Snoopers after a random delay below MAX_RESPONSE_DELAY.

messages.label: Termination
messages.note: Sent when multicast forwarding stops on the interface.
